note: Art direction for Hui Hai (HH1), chosen by the owner on 2026-09-27: the Hàng Trống folk painting 'White Tiger' (Bạch hổ), Hanoi, traditional design (public domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:White_tiger_Hang_Trong.jpg). The owner's bar: a real hand-made painting in the tiger's own bright, saturated gouache-and-watercolour look, never cute game art. The Hui Hai are drawn as tiny spirit folk in leaf clothes, never as a picture of the Ba Na people. After drawing, run python tools/bleed_colour.py on each new picture: it makes the colour spill past the ink lines, a little off register, like the hand-coloured original.
style:
A painting in EXACTLY the look of the reference image, the Vietnamese Hàng Trống folk painting of the White Tiger: the same luminous, vibrant colours and the same brightness, opaque gouache and watercolour on paper, soft and chalky, bright but not neon. A flat, mid cerulean-cobalt ground, a little mottled with uneven brushing. Swirling cloud scrolls in hot pink, emerald green, orange and lemon yellow with white edges along the top, and a red sun. Big bold simple shapes, few elements, the figure large in the picture.
COLOUR ON THE FIGURES, as on the tiger: every figure is painted in SEVERAL solid colours laid down as larger flat splotches, not one pale colour with an outline. Like the tiger's green eyes, lilac-grey crown, red tongue and green-and-red disc, put strong, surprising accents in unexpected places: green or yellow-green eyes, a patch of lilac-grey or slate in the hair, a solid leaf-green garment with a bright red sash, a yellow or orange flower tucked somewhere, a dab of turquoise, strokes of another colour dashed across a shape where you would not expect them. Cream-white is only one of the colours, for skin and a few areas. Pink and vermilion edging appears only on SOME edges, here and there, never as an outline around everything. Leaves and fern fronds are painted as solid areas of green, olive, yellow-green and teal (some with a red or yellow stroke), not pale leaves with a coloured outline. Rocks are rough orange-ochre shapes blotched with dark brown, no 3D shading.
THE HAND OF THE PAINTER: Hàng Trống pictures were printed as black woodblock outlines and coloured by hand, fast, by village painters, so colour and line never quite line up: colour patches are offset from their outlines and spill over them, the blue was brushed roughly around the figures, colours bleed into each other with soft wet edges, pigment pools and blots, and brush strokes turn up in unexpected places. Outlines are coarse and uneven, thick and thin, sometimes broken. Few strokes: fur, hair and leaf veins are a handful of loose dashes, not fine hatching. Faces are five or six brush marks (two eyes, brows, a dot of a nose, a red mouth, two cheek dabs), no shading; an old face gets two or three wrinkle dashes. Slightly soft focus, like an old photograph of the painting. Never crisp, never neat, never delicate.
Do not draw a tiger or a cat and do not copy the reference's composition. The Hui Hai are tiny forest spirits of Vietnam's Central Highlands, drawn close up so the figure fills much of the picture, with fern leaves and pebbles shown huge beside them to tell their small size; they wear clothes of woven leaves; never a picture of any real people or their dress. A real hand-made painting, not digital illustration, not a cartoon, not anime, no big eyes, no glossy or 3D rendering. Absolutely no text, letters, Chinese characters, seals, stamps or watermarks.
BRIGHTNESS AND BALANCE: keep the whole picture as light and bright as the reference, where the big white tiger fills much of it. The figure has large LIGHT areas (cream-white skin, pale yellow-green and pale lilac) broken by solid splotches of strong colour. Greens are bright spring green, yellow-green, jade and turquoise, never dark olive or forest green, and they are laid on as broad soft wet patches of colour, not as fine hatched fronds. Rocks are a bright light orange-ochre.

families.Hui Hai: Background: the cobalt ground and many-coloured cloud scrolls of the reference, a red sun, one or two huge fern fronds painted in solid greens, a stem of bamboo and a few rough ochre pebbles.

subjects.HH1-H01-kitten: the littlest Hui Hai: a tiny girl spirit in a dress of woven leaves painted in patches of bright yellow-green and jade with a bright red sash, her lilac-grey hair in a tuft tied with a yellow grass blade and an orange flower, pushing with both arms a rough ochre boulder many times her size, beside one huge fern frond. Her face is an old Vietnamese folk-painting face: round and flat, two small almond eyes with GREEN irises, arched thin brows, a tiny red mouth, pink cheek dabs; a calm, simple expression.
subjects.HH1-H01-bigcat: the littlest Hui Hai: a tiny girl spirit in a dress of woven leaves painted in patches of bright yellow-green and jade with a bright red sash, lilac-grey hair tied with a yellow grass blade and an orange flower, standing proudly on top of a rough ochre boulder in a stream, holding a pebble high over her head in one hand, the stream drawn as bands of white and turquoise wave lines, one huge fern frond bowing over her. Her face is an old Vietnamese folk-painting face: round and flat, two small almond eyes with GREEN irises, arched thin brows, a tiny red mouth, pink cheek dabs; a calm, simple expression.
subjects.HH1-D01: a Hui Hai of the stream: a tiny boy spirit in a cape of broad fern leaves painted in patches of bright yellow-green and jade with a turquoise tie, spiky slate-grey hair, green eyes, crouched on a rough ochre rock in a stream drawn as bands of white and turquoise wave lines, flicking a splash of water at a small red-and-orange fish.
subjects.HH1-D02: Yă Hui Hai, Lady of the Ferns: a tiny OLD woman spirit, clearly a grandmother, white hair in a bun with a red berry pin, green eyes, a calm, dignified, slightly stern face, wrapped in a shawl woven of moss in patches of bright jade, spring green and turquoise with a few yellow and red strokes, sitting in the coil of one huge unfurling fern frond painted in patches of spring green and yellow-green, one hand resting on a big rough ochre rock beside her.
subjects.HH1-D03: no full figure: a single pebble landing with a little white splash of dust beside a big muddy human footprint and a dropped woven bamboo carrying basket tipped on its side on rough light ochre ground, as if someone just ran off; at the side one huge fern frond painted in patches of spring green and yellow-green, and in a gap between its leaflets two tiny round green eyes of an unseen little spirit, clearly eyes in a shadowy gap of the leaves, not birds. No sandals, no shoes.
